name: Next One's Mine
tagline: You'll take anything on for anyone. Except a favour.
epigraph: The vermouth in this glass is there because hardly anyone stopped after the first.
glassware: tall glass (highball, about 350 ml), filled with ice
language_row: Wren's Resonance (v3, held on v4): Barnum check passes (the habit paired with "put it on me", a deliberate taking-on and the repayment named); sibling swap distinct from *Off Duty*, *Four Shares*, the Warrior, the Auteur, the Healer, the Angel, the Craftsman; echo grep clear ("by Friday", "by heart", "let them have" avoided); lint overlaps with *The Other Kindness* ("two dashes of bitters"), *The Other Berry* ("what you give people", "What you can't…") and an Explorer pour ("worth far more than") rewritten; every "he" is Barney Gallant (accepted by Wren). ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/barney-gallant.md` (Gary Regan, *The Joy of Mixology* pdf 59–60, relaying Stanley Walker, *The Night Club Era*; Harry Ransom Center, *Bookshop Door*; Village Preservation). *Oxford Companion*: COCKTAIL pdf 490 (rounds, the vermouth answer to strength), MANHATTAN pdf 1224 (1882 reference, 1:1 in the 1880s–90s books, rye or bourbon), MARTINI pdf 1244 (Byron, 1884), HIGHBALL pdf 1006, VERMOUTH pdf 2090, 2093, 2096. Craft: *Cocktail Codex* pp. 72, 199–202 (the Americano); *Flavor Matrix* Grain pdf 136, Grape pdf 140, pdf 132 (consulted, set aside). Room notes: `work/hero-caregiver/`.
names_note: **Next One's Mine**, the room's pick (all three, settled round 6). Also considered: *I Owe You* (Wren's round-4 pick, second; goes to Robin as the alternative), *Let Off*, *Half the Weight*, *On Me* (Wren); *Owe Me One*, *IOU*, *Even Split* (Tomás); *Half Measures* set aside (opens like *Half a Rim*). The names crossed in round 5 (each moved to the other's) and settled on Wren's reasoning: the name recognises the guest, the closing line carries the turn.
open_items: **Spark rule:** no *Flavor Matrix* spark. Grain (pdf 136) and Grape (pdf 140) share honey and nuts; honey is *Off Duty*'s, the closest sibling. The interest is the Manhattan's 1880s–90s equal split made long, with the split in plain sight. Robin's call (see memory: no spark is fine if the drink is interesting).

**Library gap:** Stanley Walker, *The Night Club Era* (1933), lending-only on archive.org. It would settle who owned the Greenwich Village Inn (Regan: Gallant's; HRC: a partner; Village Preservation: the manager), the time served, the year Club Gallant opened, and might say what the Inn poured. Also Madelon Powers, *Faces along the Bar* (rounds in 1919, unread).
**Inference owned:** that the waiters went free is inferred (the page gives the condition, not the outcome); it lives only inside the reading's signposted "I've always wondered".

**Kept out:** every "first jailed / arrested / prosecuted" claim (three sources, three versions); the 1945 Manhattan Club tale (pdf 1221, "simply not true"); Gallant's motive (legend); the 1924 club's house rules (dossier only).

**Dossier note:** the Resonance section still quotes the v2 line "it's worth far more than you ever let them tell you"; the guest text now reads "counts for more than you'll ever let anyone say" (v3 lint fix).
